title: Producer–Consumer: When a Thread Needs to Wait
topic: Producer–consumer with condition variables — a bounded buffer fills and drains; a producer that finds the buffer full waits on a condition; a consumer that finds it empty waits on the other; signal wakes one waiter

beats.narration: A producer is filling a small buffer. A consumer is draining it. What happens when one runs ahead of the other?

elements.content: One fills, one empties — when do they wait?

beats.narration: The shared buffer holds at most four items. The producer puts items in; the consumer takes them out. Both run as their own threads.

elements.content: Four empty slots in a row, producer label on left, consumer on right
Producer thread (left) drops tokens into slots one by one — slots 1..4 fill up
Consumer thread (right) pulls a token out — front slot empties

beats.narration: Now the producer wants to add a fifth item. The buffer is full — there is nowhere to put it. So the producer waits on the not-full condition.

elements.content: Buffer shown full (4 of 4); producer holds a fifth token; arrow blocked
the producer parks itself — no busy wait, no spin

beats.narration: The consumer takes an item, freeing a slot — and signals the not-full condition. The producer wakes up, drops its item in, and life goes on.

elements.content: Consumer pulls token from front; buffer goes from 4 down to 3; arrow back to producer labeled 'signal'
Producer wakes, drops its held token into the free slot — buffer back to 4

beats.narration: Two conditions, two waits, two signals — the buffer fills, drains, fills again, and neither thread ever has to spin checking a flag.

elements.content: threads sleep when they can't progress, and wake when they can
